name: ZZ Plant
description: The ZZ Plant is a tough, popular houseplant known for its glossy leaves. It contains microscopic, needle-shaped crystals called insoluble calcium oxalates. These crystals are a physical irritant, not a chemical poison. They are found throughout the entire plant. When a cat bites or chews on a ZZ Plant, these sharp crystals are released and poke the sensitive tissues of the mouth, tongue, and throat. This causes immediate discomfort and pain. The initial pain usually stops the cat from eating a large amount, so severe poisoning is rare. Symptoms are typically mild and limited to the mouth area. Look for signs like drooling, pawing at the mouth, or a reluctance to eat. In some cases, vomiting may occur. While not life-threatening, it is uncomfortable, so it's best to keep the plant out of reach. If symptoms seem severe or don't improve, contact your veterinarian.
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: insoluble calcium oxalate raphides; the waxy leaf surface provides some physical barrier but does not eliminate the toxin
Mechanism: crystals cause mechanical irritation to the oral and GI mucosa; proteolytic enzymes in sap may amplify the reaction
Symptoms: drooling, vomiting, diarrhea; oral pain is often less pronounced than with Dieffenbachia due to the thicker leaf surface
The plant’s durability and popularity mean it is very commonly found in homes and offices
Monitor for GI symptoms if ingestion occurs; contact your vet if vomiting is persistent

symptoms.name: Mouth irritation (intense pain and burning sensation in the mouth)
symptoms.notes: This irritation is caused by the mechanical trauma of insoluble calcium oxalate crystals (raphides) piercing the oral tissues when the plant is chewed. The immediate and intense pain usually deters the cat from swallowing or eating large quantities of the plant.

symptoms.name: Excessive drooling (hypersalivation)
symptoms.notes: This is a direct physiological response to the sharp crystals irritating the delicate mucous membranes in the cat's mouth and throat.

symptoms.name: Reluctance to eat (anorexia)
symptoms.notes: Cats will often refuse food due to the lingering pain and inflammation in their oral cavity. Rinsing the cat's mouth with water can help soothe the irritation, but if the refusal to eat persists, veterinary consultation is recommended.

symptoms.name: Vomiting
symptoms.notes: Vomiting can occur if the cat manages to swallow the plant material. While typically a mild and self-limiting symptom for this plant, a veterinarian should be consulted if the vomiting becomes continuous.
